Probes — how monitors work

The shared engine behind Deep monitors and Service Monitor — creating, discovering, running, muting and charting probes, how statuses and thresholds are decided, and how long history is kept.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereMonitoring → Deep monitors (URL /monitoring/deep/) and Monitoring → Service Monitor (URL /monitoring/services/)

What is it?#

A probe is one check against one thing — a URL, a device's CPU, a server policy's sessions, a FortiAuthenticator licence pool — that runs on a schedule, grades the result (ok, warn, crit, error, unknown) and stores every result as a time series.

Two pages show probes: Deep monitors (checks that reach into the box: synthetic HTTPS, interfaces, CPU, memory, proxyd) and Service Monitor (telemetry read over the appliance's REST monitor API). They are two views of one subsystem: same storage, same runner, same deep_monitor scheduled action. This article covers what they share.

What does it do?#

  • Runs each enabled probe when its interval has elapsed, as part of the deep_monitor sweep.
  • Stores a sample per run (status, value, detail, raw payload) and keeps hourly and daily roll-ups for long charts.
  • Feeds the Deep monitors signal of Device health, the device findings of Alerting, Analytics rule panels and Monitoring reports.
  • Lets you create probes by hand or discover them from a device, mute one temporarily, and open a chart of any probe.

Requirements#

  • At least one registered appliance (a bare URL probe on Deep monitors needs none).
  • The deep_monitor scheduled action (Deep monitors — probe sweep) for automatic runs. It is in the standard seed plan at every 3 minutes; a fresh install has none until you seed or create it — see Scheduled actions.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

  • Viewing probes, charts and history: the legacy view gate — any read permission, for example monitoring.view; all system profiles have it. A custom profile with no read key gets 403.
  • Discover from device, Add probe, Probe now, edit, enable/disable, unmute and delete: the legacy config_write gate (for example operations.apply or appliances.apply; full list in Monitoring overview). Without it these buttons are not rendered and the endpoints return 403.
  • Each page only accepts its own kinds: a probe id that belongs to the other page answers 404 (no such probe on this page).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: viewing probes now requires a read permission instead of sign-in alone; new probes default to a 3-minute interval, and muted probes get an Unmute action on their row.

How to use#

Discover probes from a device#

  1. Click Discover from device.
  2. Pick the device and tick the sets you want (they differ per page — see Deep monitors and Service Monitor).
  3. Click Discover. A job runs in the background; the result (N service probe(s) (M already present) …) arrives in the notification bell and the table reloads.

Discovery is idempotent: probes that already exist are left alone.

Add or edit a probe by hand#

  1. Click Add probe (or the pencil icon on a row).
  2. Choose the Type, give it a Name, pick the Device, and fill the fields for that type.
  3. Set Interval (min) (default 3, the seeded sweep interval) and Timeout (s).
  4. Optionally mute it (see below).
  5. Click Save.

Run probes now#

  • Probe now in the header runs every enabled probe of this page for the devices visible in this ADOM.
  • The play icon on a row runs that one probe.

Both run as a background job. A successful run is silent (the table reloads); a failed sweep sends <page> sweep failed: … to the bell.

Mute a probe#

In the edit form, set Mute this probe (hours) (maximum 720) and a reason (why (recorded and shown on the row)), then Save. The row shows a muted chip. To lift it early, click the bell icon (Unmute) on the row; it appears only on muted probes and is recorded in the audit log. Editing the probe and setting the hours to 0 or empty also works.

A muted probe keeps running and keeps its own status; it stops raising the device badge and the alert mail. There is no permanent mute.

Read history#

  • Click a sparkline to open the chart: 1 h, 24 h, 7 days, 30 days, or From date / To date and Apply. The chart draws threshold lines and states which source it used (raw, hourly, daily).
  • Click the Last result text to open History: the last 200 samples and the Latest raw payload.

Enable, disable, delete#

Use the pause/play and trash icons on the row. A disabled probe is greyed and not run by the sweep.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Type The probe kind; each page offers only its own kinds Yes Processor load
Name Free text, up to 120 characters; defaults to the URL or kind No fweb-01 · shop CPU
Device Appliance to measure. Every kind except a bare URL probe needs one Mostly fweb-01
Interval (min) Minimum minutes between runs (minimum 1; default 3) Yes 3
Timeout (s) Per-run timeout (minimum 1) Yes 10
Thresholds Kind-specific (see the two page articles). Empty = inherit the product value from Settings → Thresholds; 0 = level switched off No 85
Mute this probe (hours) 0–720; with a reason No 48 / "migration leftover"

❗Important — Interval and the sweep

A probe only runs when its own interval has elapsed and the sweep ticks. With the seeded 3-minute sweep, a 5-minute probe actually runs every 6 minutes. New probes (hand-made or discovered) default to 3 minutes; existing probes keep the interval they were saved with. Use multiples of the sweep interval. The Collection cadence button on Analytics lists declared versus effective cadence for every probe.

Status values#

Status Meaning
ok measured, within limits
warn / crit a threshold or a binary fact was crossed
error the probe could not execute (refused, timed out, unparsable output, kind not supported on that product)
unknown never run, or nothing measurable (for example a counter without a ceiling)

Example#

🧪Example — Watch CPU on a new FortiWeb with the product defaults

  1. Discover from device → fweb-02 → keep Device baseline ticked → Discover.
  2. The bell reports baseline: interface, cpu, memory, proxyd.
  3. The CPU probe's warn/crit boxes are empty, so it inherits the FortiWeb values from Settings → Thresholds. Raise the FortiWeb CPU limit there and this probe follows immediately.

Result#

  • Creating, editing, toggling, unmuting and deleting a probe writes an audit entry (deep_monitor.create, service_monitor.update, …).
  • Each run stores one sample and updates the probe's last status.
  • The worst enabled, non-muted probe of a device becomes the Deep monitors signal on Device health and is mailed by the alert engine.

Troubleshooting#

"'<kind>' is not a Deep monitors probe kind" / "… is not a Service Monitor probe kind"#

You submitted a kind that belongs to the other page. Create it there.

"<Kind> cannot be measured on <product> — supported: …"#

The kind does not apply to that product (for example proxyd on a FortiADC). Pick a supported kind or device.

"an HTTPS probe needs a URL" / "a <kind> probe needs a device"#

Fill the missing field.

"the critical threshold must be at or above the warning one"#

Make critical ≥ warning, or set one of them to 0 to disable that level.

"nothing to run"#

Probe now found no enabled probe on this page in this ADOM. Enable or create probes first.

Probes stay "unknown" / never update#

Possible causes — no deep_monitor schedule; the device is in maintenance (scheduled runs skip it, Probe now still runs it).

Solution — create the schedule (every 3 minutes) or take the device out of maintenance.

Verification — the Checked column shows a recent time.

Advanced#

Advanced Storage and retention
  • Probes live in monitor_probe, samples in monitor_sample.
  • Raw samples are capped per probe (default 500, minimum 10; field retention). Before pruning, each run folds samples into roll-ups: hourly kept 90 days, daily kept 730 days (min/avg/max). Charts pick the source per range and say which one they drew. A custom chart range is capped at 731 days.
Advanced Threshold resolution and binary facts

Each limit resolves in order: the probe's own value → the product scope's value (Settings → Thresholds) → the shipped default. Binary facts have per-product severities (critical / warning / off) set on the same page; off changes the grade but the fact is still printed. Shipped defaults:

Fact Default
Every backend of a server policy is down crit
Some backends of a server policy are down warn
A pool member has no health check configured warn
Server policy is administratively disabled warn
Server policy membership changed warn
The proxy daemon is not running crit
The proxy daemon's PID set changed warn
A monitored interface changed IP or link state crit
A monitored interface vanished from the harvest crit
Transaction counter reads zero while the policy carries traffic warn
Advanced Sweep behaviour
  • The scheduled sweep skips probes whose appliance is in maintenance; a manual Probe now does not.
  • An exception inside a probe becomes an error sample; one broken probe never stops the sweep.
  • Probe now with no selection is limited to this page's kinds and this ADOM's devices.
